summary.headline: Adani Total Gas Q2 FY27 volumes rose 12% YoY to 315 MMSCM and EBITDA 12% to INR340 crore, while PAT grew only 3% to INR167 crore amid a 43% gas cost surge.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 volumes grew 12% YoY to 315 MMSCM, with CNG up 17% and PNG up 3%, and EBITDA rose 12% to INR340 crore on revenue up 34% to INR2,102 crore. Natural gas costs rose 43% YoY on higher Brent and LNG prices, currency depreciation and lower domestic gas availability, which compressed EBITDA margin to about 16.2%. Management said it passed on part of the cost through calibrated CNG price hikes and a long-term gas contract. H1 FY27 volumes grew 13% to 618 MMSCM and EBITDA rose 3% to INR621 crore. Management is expanding CNG stations, households, industrial connections and EV charging, and is scaling CBG.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume 223 MMSCM, up 17% YoY; network at 723 CNG stations after 16 added in the quarter. Management targets 80-90 CNG stations in FY27 versus about 68 added in FY26.

segments.name: PNG (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume 92 MMSCM, up 3% YoY; 39,574 new household connections in the quarter, taking PNG households to 11.81 lakh. Management aims for more than 2 lakh connections in FY27.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: About 900 new customers added in H1 FY27, taking the base to 10,864, roughly 1.4x the full FY26 additions. New geographies contributed 41% of volume mix versus 35% a year earlier.

segments.name: EV charging
segments.commentary: 5,513 charging points installed across 26 states/UTs and 225 cities, with 63 MW installed capacity. Focus is shifting to B2B charging for group companies, including Adani Cement, Adani Ports and Adani Logistics trucks.

segments.name: CBG
segments.commentary: One operating plant at Barsana (UP), producing about 5-6 tonnes a day, with expansion to double output in 5-6 months; technology tie-up with Thermax is done and investment is committed. Other projects are being evaluated at a slower pace.

guidance_outlook: CNG station additions targeted at 80-90 in FY27, and FY28 expected to be similar or more aggressive, subject to planning.
PNG domestic connections targeted above 2 lakh in FY27.
About 70 CNG stations under advanced construction, with equipment procurement started and pipeline laying underway.
Management expects FY28 infrastructure expansion at a similar pace to FY27; no capex figure was given.
Management called margin pressure temporary and said it will pursue long-term gas contracts where they support better EBITDA margins.
capex_capacity: Steel pipeline network at 16,305 inch-km at end Q2 FY27, after 732 inch-km added in H1 FY27.
H1 FY27: 21 CNG stations added, 77,870 new household connections, about 900 industrial/commercial customers added.
EV charging: 5,513 points installed (about 4,809 operational, per an analyst), 63 MW capacity; capex to reach the 75,000-point target was not disclosed.
Pan-India network with JV partner IOAGPL: 1,185 CNG stations, 14.31 lakh PNG households, 12,925 industrial/commercial connections, 29,156 inch-km pipeline.
Total capex for FY27 and FY28 was not quantified on the call.
demand_pricing: CNG prices were revised several times (June, July, August) in markets such as Ahmedabad and Faridabad; management said pricing is calibrated and does not fully pass on cost increases. An analyst cited a magnitude of about INR11-12/kg.

Gas sourcing: APM supply share was slightly lower QoQ. Spot exposure fell from about 15% of the portfolio before the term agreement to 7-8% now. Around 40% of the remaining supply is linked to markers such as Henry Hub and Brent.
HPHT gas allocated by government fluctuates 5-10% month-to-month or fortnight-to-fortnight, depending on production cycles.
Management said CNG industry demand is growing about 20%, and ATGL's CNG growth is 17-18%.
Average domestic PNG consumption is about 0.4 SCMD per household.

qa_highlights.question: Have CNG price hikes restored pre-war margins in markets where increases were taken through August, with an INR11-12/kg magnitude?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are calibrated and not fully passed on. Long-term gas contracts helped contain the increase, and Ahmedabad and Faridabad are key markets where increases are weighed against cost pressure. No margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the APM share and the composition of the remaining 75% of gas supply?
qa_highlights.answer: APM share was slightly lower. Other domestic sources such as new well gas and HPHT fluctuate. Spot share fell from about 15% to 7-8%, and about 40% of supply is linked to Henry Hub or Brent markers.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CNG station and capex plans for the next two quarters, FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CNG station additions are targeted at 80-90 in FY27 versus 68 in FY26, and FY28 is expected to be similar or more aggressive. No capex figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins return to the historical 23%+ level, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is within its control, and the margin pressure from West Asia and Brent volatility is temporary. It is pursuing long-term contracts, and no timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EV charger utilisation levels, capex to reach 75,000 points, and the timeline to EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The focus is on B2B charging with group companies and truck routes to raise utilisation above B2C levels. No utilisation percentage, capex figure or EBITDA timeline was provided.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CBG expansion plans, feedstock, technology partners and economics, including GOBARdhan?
qa_highlights.answer: The Barsana plant uses cow dung and paddy straw with Thermax as technology partner, producing 5-6 tonnes/day and expanding to double in 5-6 months. Other projects are being evaluated slowly, with feedstock and land as the key constraints. Economics were not discussed.

risks_watch: Gas cost pressure: natural gas cost up 43% YoY; margin recovery depends on the pace of pass-through and the share of long-term contracts.
Domestic gas allocation volatility: HPHT and APM allocations vary 5-10% and may shift further.
EBITDA margin about 16.2% in Q2 FY27 versus a historical 23%+; PAT grew only 3% against EBITDA growth of 12%.
EV charging utilisation is low and the 75,000-point target is far off; capex and returns were not disclosed.
CBG scale-up depends on feedstock availability and technology; the plant is small, and further projects are deferred.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, network growth and execution, but defensive on margins: management attributed compression to temporary gas-cost shocks. It was evasive on pricing headroom, margin timelines, EV utilisation and capex quantum.
key_quotes: By leveraging diversified sourcing and flexible procurement, we achieved a stellar 12% year-on-year increase in quarterly volumes to 315 MMSCM and matching 12% increase in EBITDA to INR340 crores.
Now these temporary issues, whether it is West Asia crisis, whether it is volatility in the Brent or all other markers, so these are temporary in nature.
And we are very much keen and we are very much focused in terms of development of PNG for households and our key areas as well as our new GAs.
